JNJ.rationale: JNJ is a high-quality healthcare franchise with durable cash generation, a 50+ year dividend streak, and an active pipeline refresh (Carvykti +62% YoY, TALVEY Phase 3 data, Firefly Bio acquisition). However, the stock has re-rated to peak multiples on flat-to-declining fundamentals, creating a deeply unfavorable risk/reward. PE of 28.5x sits at the absolute top of the 365-day range (16.9–28.5), representing 69% multiple expansion in 12 months with no corresponding earnings growth. Normalized EPS of ~$8.55 (excluding the anomalous Q1 one-time item) confirms the market is paying peak multiples for a flat-earnings business. Net margin has compressed from 27.3% to 21.8%, operating margin declined from 31.2% (Q3) to 24.9% (Q4), and Q4 operating cash flow collapsed 72.6% QoQ to $2.51B. The earnings yield of 3.5% sits 90bp below the 10-year Treasury yield of 4.4%, implying a negative equity risk premium. Cost-of-revenue surged 11.1% QoQ in Q4 despite flat revenue. Stelara patent cliff is accelerating faster than expected, with additional LOEs for Simponi and Opsumit in 2026. FTC antitrust action on Stelara adds regulatory overhang. Talc litigation (75,000+ lawsuits, $32M recent verdict) remains unresolved. A reversion to the median PE of ~19.5x on normalized EPS of $8.55 implies ~$167, a 32% drawdown. The qualitative franchise quality is real but fully priced and then some — the market has 'spent' the multiple expansion without earnings growth to show for it. All three pillars align bearishly: deteriorating margin/cash trajectory, peak valuation vs own history, and no near-term fundamental catalyst to justify the premium.
